subject: On-prem observability: SIEM ingestion & trace-hook checklist
messages:
From: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@acmebank.com>

Subject: Observability for Redwood Private (on‑prem) — SIEM ingestion questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team is building the SIEM ingestion plan for the pilot in our on‑prem data center and we need a concrete list of options and the exact network/format requirements so we can put this in our procurement and firewall change requests. Specifically:

- Which log export modes do you support from Redwood Private (syslog/TCP TLS, HTTPS HEC, S3 delivery, Kafka)?
- Are there recommended forwarders (Fluentd/Fluent Bit/OpenTelemetry Collector) and any prebuilt configs?
- What IPs/domains/ports does our egress policy need to allow?
- How are traces exported? Do you support OTLP/Jaeger/Splunk APM?
- Any encryption/KMS/HSM constraints for trace/log metadata?

Can you also attach a short playbook or checklist we can hand to our ops team (firewall team + SIEM integrators)? We'd like a one‑page runbook and an example OTLP config to start with.

Appreciate your help — want to get this scheduled before our audit window in mid‑Dec.

Thanks,
Thomas Lee\Security Engineer, Acme Bank
attachments: requested: playbook checklist, OTLP sample

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@acmebank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability for Redwood Private (on‑prem) — SIEM ingestion questions

Thomas —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise options matrix and a recommended checklist for the pilot. I'm attaching a short playbook PDF, a CSV of our published egress IPs for the Dedicated/private forwarder, and an example OTLP collector YAML (see attachments).

Quick options summary (what Redwood Private supports):
- Syslog over TLS (RFC 5425) to external collectors: supported via built‑in forwarder or customer‑managed Fluentd/Fluent Bit.
- HTTPS push (Splunk HEC / custom HTTP endpoints): supported; HEC token auth over TLS.
- S3/GCS object sink: asynchronous delivery for bulk logs/archives (useful for long‑term retention).
- Kafka topic exports: supported for high‑throughput environments behind customer VPCs.
- OTLP/Jaeger traces: we expose OTLP/grpc from the local collector; can forward to Jaeger/OTLP endpoints or convert to Splunk/Zipkin formats.

Security/network constraints and recommendations:
- Egress: allow outbound to our forwarder IPs (attachments: network-egress-ips.csv) or allow to your chosen collector host:port. For syslog TLS use TCP/6514 by default; HEC/HTTPS uses 443.
- TLS: mTLS is supported for syslog/HTTP where customer provides certs; otherwise TLS1.2+ with server cert validation.
- KMS: payload encryption at rest uses customer KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM via KMIP in private deployments). For PCI/PHI customers we recommend KMS + HSM for signing.
- Data flow: logs -> local forwarder (sidecar or agent) -> OTLP/HEC/Kafka/S3 -> SIEM. Traces: application span -> local OTLP collector -> sampling -> export to your APM/OTLP endpoint.

Minimum checklist for your firewall/ops team (pilot):
1) Allow outbound TCP 6514 to the collector host (if using syslog TLS) or TCP 443 for HTTPS/HEC.
2) If using our managed forwarder endpoint, allow outbound to the IPs in network-egress-ips.csv and the TLS hostnames in the playbook.
3) Provision a HEC token or client cert for auth; share certs via secure channel (we support S/MIME or pre-shared S3 object).
4) Confirm OTLP endpoint details and sampling policy; we recommend 1–5% sampling for pilot tracing, full sampling for rare critical flows.
5) Verify retention & retention export: configure S3 bucket for archive exports if you want raw logs retained beyond 90 days.

Attachment notes:
- redwood-private-siem-playbook.pdf: 2‑page playbook with diagrams, sample NACL rules, and step‑by‑step validation checks.
- network-egress-ips.csv: single column list of IPs we publish for the forwarder gateway.
- otlp-trace-example.yaml: sample OpenTelemetry Collector config to forward to OTLP/Jaeger and to export spans to Splunk.

Action items from our side: we'll run a short validation with your SIEM team against a staging collector. Can Neha (cc'd) own the validation run? Sergio will confirm the OTLP sampling defaults for this customer.

Proposed next step: 30‑minute sync Thursday 11/19 10am PT — I can share our staging collector for a live ingest test.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer\Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Validation: Redwood will send 10k synthetic events and 1k spans to the staging collector during the Thursday test. Neha will post the ingest report and event field map.

2) Tomorrow 11/19 10:00am PT: 30m validation call (staging collector live ingest). Join link: https://meet.redwood.ai/obs‑sync/20261119 (will send calendar invite).
